- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially after sharp dips.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >72.5), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% per day.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., from 76+ to 70–72), model often fails to correct; add a “reversion buffer” to forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent trend; use 18-day history as anchor, not 30-day trend, to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome deviates >3% from forecast in first 3 days, model is likely lagging; adjust early forecast upward if sentiment is bullish, downward if bearish.
